meaning.en: To annoy, irritate or upset someone, especially repeatedly or in a way that is difficult for that person to ignore.
meaning.zh: 令某人感到煩躁、惱火或心煩，尤其指某種言行反覆出現，令人難以忽視。

register.summaryEn: everyday conversations; messages between friends or colleagues; interviews; personal stories; general workplace discussion; informal articles and commentary.
register.summaryZh: 這個表達屬於非正式至中性語域，常見於日常對話、朋友或同事之間的訊息、訪問、個人敘述及一般工作討論。
register.formalEn: In a very formal complaint, report or official letter, annoy, irritate, cause frustration or cause concern may be more suitable.
register.formalZh: 在非常正式的投訴信、報告或官方文件中，使用 annoy、irritate、cause frustration 或 cause concern 有時會更合適。

benefits.titleZh: 表達持續而難以忽視的煩躁
benefits.en: The idiom is useful when something does not merely annoy somebody once, but continues to occupy their attention.
benefits.zh: 這個慣用語適合描述某件事不只是惹人煩躁一次，而是持續令人介意。

benefits.titleEn: It Expresses a Personal Emotional Reaction
benefits.en: Different people may be annoyed by different things. The possessive form clearly identifies whose feelings are affected. That noise gets under my skin, but it does not bother my sister.
benefits.zh: 不同的人可能會被不同事情惹惱。 所有格可以清楚指出是誰受到情緒影響。 那種噪音令我十分心煩，但我的妹妹並不介意。

examples.en: That noise gets under my skin, but it does not bother my sister.
examples.zh: 那種噪音令我十分心煩，但我的妹妹並不介意。

benefits.en: The expression can show that somebody is intentionally saying or doing something to produce an emotional reaction. He is only trying to get under your skin.
benefits.zh: 這個表達可以指出某人故意說話或做事，以引起另一個人的情緒反應。 他只是想故意惹惱你。

examples.en: He is only trying to get under your skin.

benefits.titleEn: It Is Useful for Advice About Self-Control
benefits.titleZh: 適合用來勸人保持冷靜
benefits.en: Do not let it get under your skin is a natural way to advise somebody not to give an irritating person the reaction they want.
benefits.zh: Do not let it get under your skin 是一種自然的勸告方式，提醒別人不要因惱人的言行而失去冷靜。

benefits.en: His repeated comments are getting under my skin.
benefits.zh: 這個慣用語把「持續惹惱」和「難以忽視」兩層意思集中在一個表達之中。

benefits.titleEn: It Is Not Automatically Better Than “Annoy”
benefits.titleZh: 並非在所有情況下都比 annoy 更好
benefits.en: Use the idiom when the personal and continuing nature of the irritation matters. In formal or emotionally neutral writing, annoy or cause frustration may be clearer.
benefits.zh: 當持續而個人化的煩躁感十分重要時，可以使用這個慣用語。 在正式或客觀的文章中，annoy 或 cause frustration 可能更清楚。

origin.statusEn: Exact Origin Unknown; Gradual Metaphorical Development
origin.statusZh: 確切來源不明；逐漸形成比喻意思

history.en: The exact first idiomatic use has not been firmly identified. However, the negative figurative meaning was clearly established by the early twentieth century. Mary Roberts Rinehart’s 1920 novel A Poor Wise Man includes a character saying that a political idea “gets under my skin”, meaning that it strongly irritates him.
history.zh: 這個慣用語的確切首次用法尚未能確認。 不過，到了二十世紀初，以它表示煩躁的比喻意思已經相當明確。 Mary Roberts Rinehart 在1920年的小說《A Poor Wise Man》中，便讓一名角色說某個政治觀念「gets under my skin」，意思是那個觀念令他十分惱火。

history.en: A physical irritation beneath the skin is difficult to escape or ignore. Speakers gradually applied the same image to words, habits and people that remain in the mind and continue causing annoyance. This is the most plausible general explanation, although no single moment of creation has been proved.
history.zh: 皮膚下的刺激令人難以擺脫或忽視。 後來，說話者逐漸把相同畫面用於某些說話、習慣或人物：它們會一直留在腦海中，持續令人煩躁。 這是最合理的一般解釋，但目前沒有證據證明這個表達在某一個確切時刻被創造。

origin.memoryEn: Something irritating under the skin is hard to ignore; an irritating person or habit can feel equally difficult to ignore.
origin.memoryZh: 皮膚下的刺激難以忽視；一個惱人的人或習慣也可能同樣令人無法不去介意。

rules.en: The expression needs an appropriately inflected form of get.
rules.zh: 這個慣用語必須配合適當形式的 get。

rules.titleEn: Match the Possessive Form to the Annoyed Person
rules.titleZh: 規則二：所有格必須配合感到煩躁的人
rules.en: The comments get under his skin. ✗
rules.zh: 如果感到煩躁的人是「我」，便必須使用 my skin。

rules.titleZh: 規則三：skin 必須使用單數
rules.en: Even when several people are annoyed, the fixed expression normally keeps skin singular.
rules.zh: 即使感到煩躁的人不只一位，skin 通常仍保持單數。

rules.titleZh: 規則五：保留時態及確定程度
rules.en: Do not change might get into got. This would change a possibility into a fact.
rules.zh: 不要把 might get 改成 got，否則會把可能性變成已發生的事實。

rules.titleZh: 規則六：只用於真正令人煩躁的情況
rules.en: The source must support a noticeable emotional reaction.
rules.zh: 原句必須真正支持明顯的煩躁或惱火情緒。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for Serious Medical Conditions
rules.titleZh: 規則七：不要用於嚴重醫療情況
rules.en: The expression is too informal and too weak for describing serious illness, injury or medical danger.
rules.zh: 這個表達不適合用來描述嚴重疾病、受傷或醫療危險。

rules.titleZh: 規則八：避免意外使用字面意思
rules.en: Literal: Idiomatic: Only the second sentence uses the target idiom.
rules.zh: 醫生把藥物注入病人的皮下。 病人反覆投訴，令護士感到煩躁。 只有第二句使用了本課教授的慣用語。

examples.en: The patient’s repeated complaints got under the nurse’s skin.
examples.zh: 病人反覆投訴，令護士感到煩躁。

rules.titleZh: 規則九：單獨使用 under the skin 意思不同
rules.en: Under the skin may literally mean beneath the skin or figuratively mean beneath outward appearances or at heart.
rules.zh: 單獨使用時，可以指「皮膚下面」，也可以表示「在外表之下」或「本質上」。 這些都不是本練習教授的意思。

rules.titleEn: This Exercise Excludes the Positive Sense
rules.titleZh: 規則十：本練習不包括正面意思
rules.en: Some dictionaries also record a positive sense in which a person, place or work affects someone deeply or gradually becomes liked. to annoy, irritate or upset someone
rules.zh: 部分詞典亦記錄一個正面意思，表示某人、某地或某件作品深深打動一個人，或逐漸令人喜愛。 本練習只教授「令某人煩躁、惱火或心煩」這個意思。
